Oops, I may have forgotten about a repository I added that makes it show up for me. Here are the steps:

Open a terminal

sudo apt-add-repository ppa:numix/ppa

sudo apt-get update

sudo apt-get install numix-icon-theme numix-icon-theme-circle

Since you're new to Linux, I'll explain these commains in case you're not familiar with what they do. "apt" is the name of the software management system that Mint uses. Just like windows programs have little installation wizards, that's pretty much apt is doing. So the first line is telling apt about a new source of software "ppa:numix/ppa" on the internet.

The second line is telling your local machine to update itself. We want apt to know everything available in that new source.

The third line, is telling apt what you want to install. In this case "numix-icon-theme" and "numix-icon-theme-circle" are the names of the packages.
